title: Disable Submit
prompt: A React login form disables submit while saving or while required fields are empty. Write a helper that returns true if saving is true, email is empty, or password is empty.

explanation.beginner:
Example: disableSubmit({"email":"a@b.com","password":"secret"}, false) produces false. The result must follow this precise rule: A React login form disables submit while saving or while required fields are empty. Write a helper that returns true if saving is true, email is empty, or password is empty. Work with one argument at a time and distinguish the values that select a branch from the values returned by that branch.

Compare “disables while saving”: input [{"email":"a@b.com","password":"secret"},true] produces true. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.

Tempting mistake: Do not hard-code the first example: the disables while saving case changes the input contract’s boundary or shape. Compare the actual outputs rather than only checking whether both are truthy.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “disables while saving”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
